items.headline: Z.ai completes GLM-5.2 fully-open MIT weights
items.diff_narrative: A net-new open-weight model lead, with no equivalent on June 17. Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI) moved GLM-5.2 from a June 13 subscription preview to publicly downloadable Hugging Face weights under an unrestricted MIT license. The model is a roughly 753-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (about 40B active per token) with a one-million-token context held stable by an IndexShare change the lab says cuts per-token compute about 2.9x at full length, plus a multi-token-prediction layer reported to lift speculative-decoding accepted length up to 20 percent. On coding benchmarks Z.ai reports 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 against 85.0 for Claude Opus 4.8, and 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro (ahead of GPT-5.5's reported 58.6), landing second on Code Arena, already wired into 20-plus coding environments at subscription tiers around $12.60/month. Figures are vendor-reported; coverage flags that routing through Z.ai's hosted API carries China-jurisdiction data-handling considerations.

items.headline: vLLM ships v0.23.0
items.diff_narrative: A new inference-serving story with no June 17 counterpart. The vLLM project tagged v0.23.0 on June 15, folding in 408 commits from 200 contributors. The headline is broader DeepSeek-V4 maturity (improved attention kernels, MoE handling, decoupled sparse multi-head-latent-attention metadata across backends); Model Runner V2 becomes the default execution path for Llama and Mistral dense models (previously Qwen3-only) and gains a FlashInfer sampler plus breakable CUDA graphs; the Rust frontend picks up a streaming generate endpoint, dynamic LoRA loading, and more tool-call parsers. Also lands Gemma 4 support, Transformers v5 compatibility, a multi-tier KV-cache offloading framework, and new models (Step-3.7-Flash, Cosmos 3 Reasoner, JetBrains Mellum v2, Granite Speech Plus, Cohere Mini Code). Reported micro-optimizations stop short of an end-to-end throughput claim.

items.headline: MosaicQuant unified 4-bit quantization paper
items.diff_narrative: A net-new quantization-research item absent on June 17. An arXiv paper (arXiv:2606.15652, posted June 14) proposes MosaicQuant, which disaggregates each weight matrix into a dense 4-bit base plus a sparse 4-bit residual that compensates for error in the most error-sensitive blocks, keeping both pieces in 4-bit rather than reverting to mixed precision. A companion ZipperEngine folds the sparse residual into the dense 4-bit matrix operations through an overlapped pipeline to preserve a single low-bit execution path. On LLaMA3 and Qwen3 the method is reported to retain near-FP16 accuracy with up to a 1.24x speedup over the 16-bit baseline. As a single-paper result the numbers are the authors' own and await independent reproduction.

items.headline: Neura Robotics closes up-to-$1.4B Series C
items.diff_narrative: A new physical-AI funding story with no June 17 equivalent. German cognitive-robotics firm Neura Robotics disclosed a Series C of up to $1.4 billion (surfaced June 10, still driving coverage this week), which it calls the largest raise ever by a full-stack robotics company; the round is structured as a milestone-tied ceiling rather than a single check, at a valuation reported near $7 billion. The investor roster pulls chip and cloud strategics directly onto the cap table - Nvidia, Amazon, Qualcomm, Bosch, Schaeffler, the EIB, imec.xpand and Lingotto Horizon - alongside a Tether-led syndicate. Metzingen-based Neura, led by founder David Reger, earmarks the capital to scale serial production of its 4NE-1 humanoid toward multi-million units by 2030 and to roll out 'Neura Gyms' training environments, with first volume shipments targeted for late 2026.

items.headline: Bay Area AI events calendar rolls forward
items.diff_narrative: The forward-looking three-track events bullet carries forward from June 17 with the calendar advanced and closed dates dropped. The Databricks Data + AI Summit is now on its final day (June 18) and exits after this, and the June 16 AICamp documentary premiere plus the June 4 in-person Snowflake Dev Day have passed. Still-upcoming anchors are largely unchanged: Snowflake's virtual Dev Day (June 25), the AI Engineer World's Fair (June 29-July 2, the program now cited as roughly 29 tracks and around 300 speakers versus yesterday's 20-plus/250-plus, with the Cerebral Valley hackathon June 27-28), the Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24, AMD/Google/Microsoft/NVIDIA keynotes), AI Tinkerers' Offensive Security Demo Night (June 25), SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit (August 11-12), Black Hat USA's AI Summit (August 1-6), OWASP Global AppSec USA (November 5-6), AMD Advancing AI (July 23), Hot Chips (August 23-25), the AI Infra Summit (September 15-17), GitHub Universe (October 28-29), and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4). All three sub-tracks (mainstream dev/data, AI-security, AI-chip) remain covered.

items.headline: Prediction set rotates entirely to GLM-5.2 and Neura themes
items.diff_narrative: All three predictions are net-new and the June 17 set retires. Yesterday's predictions - managed model-serving platforms defaulting to safe artifact handling (Vertex AI RCE), a named hyperscaler committing Corsair-class inference silicon (d-Matrix), and production-traffic replay becoming a second pre-release eval layer (OpenAI Deployment Simulation) - all drop with their source storylines. Today's three track the new leads: an open-weight (MIT/Apache-2.0) coding model reaching 85.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 by Q4 2026, riding GLM-5.2's 81.0 plus cheaper 4-bit serving from MosaicQuant and vLLM defaults; a rival full-stack humanoid maker closing a $500M-plus round with an overlapping chip/cloud strategic by Q4 2026, off the Neura raise; and enterprises codifying a self-host-the-open-weights posture over the foreign-hosted Z.ai API on data-sovereignty grounds by Q2 2027.
